summary: Short eight-minute peer-to-peer call between two closers, Richard Claessen and Michael Brideau. Proposed subtype label: 'peer_check_in'. Michael is travelling, has just moved into a cold last-minute rental with unreliable internet, and asked Richard to help him test whether Zoom would hold up before his next prospect call; it does not, and he switches to phone hotspot. Richard gives a short day report: no close, one prospect disqualified for lack of money, one no-show rebooked for Saturday, and a long-standing prospect who works in an operating room cancelled again on him for a work emergency. They agree to run a mock call together the next day after the team meeting. Substantively this is logistics and morale, with one significant conduct disclosure.
notable: Richard stated to a colleague that no-show rates vary by prospect name and gave an ethnically-marked example, then advised Michael to phone that specific prospect ahead of the call on that basis: "No show rates with different names definitely do change. That is the fact... just people that are, like, called Abdul or something, I don't have anything against anyone, like, I like anyone, right, but, like, always a no-sure rate with those names are always higher, I don't know why, but it's whatever, I would say give them a call." Michael acted on it: "Yeah, I just sent him a message, I'll give him a call here in two minutes as well."

A prospect who has been in the CRM for roughly six months works in surgery and has now cancelled on two different closers for operating-room emergencies: "he's like in an operating room. So a couple of months ago, we canceled on a closer because he had to jump into an emergency at work. Guess what he just did with me for the same reason." Richard is confident of the close if the call ever happens: "I know when he jumps on, I'm going to close him."
Disqualification on affordability is being applied in practice, not just discussed: "I got one guy on the call. He didn't have money. So I had to disqualify him."

Michael Brideau is working from short-term rentals abroad with unverified connectivity, and lost the video connection repeatedly inside this eight-minute test — a call-quality risk that carries into prospect calls: "if it continues sucking then I'm just gonna... literally go to my friend's house and take calls there."
Peer mock-call practice is arranged informally between closers outside the manager-run training block.
